_doc: Field-wide milestones for the timeline (course-specific events live in each course.json). year < 0 means BC.

milestones.title: Oracle-bone inscriptions
milestones.detail: Shang diviners at Yinxu (modern Anyang) carve several thousand characters on turtle plastrons and ox scapulae — the earliest substantial corpus of Chinese writing.

milestones.title: Bronze inscriptions reach maturity
milestones.detail: Western Zhou ritual bronzes carry texts of up to nearly five hundred characters, fixing the graph shapes and the literary language in a monumental register.

milestones.title: Classical becomes a written standard
milestones.detail: By the Han, the spoken language had moved far from the idiom of the Five Classics, yet classical prose kept setting the norm for learned writing for the next two millennia.

milestones.title: Shuowen jiezi
milestones.detail: Xu Shen completes the first systematic dictionary: 9,353 graphs analysed under 540 radicals, establishing the radical-and-stroke method used to this day.

milestones.title: Preface to the Orchid Pavilion Collection
milestones.detail: Wang Xizhi writes the running-script draft that calligraphy ever since has treated as its supreme model of regular-cursive elegance.

milestones.title: Wenxin diaolong
milestones.detail: Liu Xie's Literary Mind and the Carving of Dragons maps genre, style, imagery and craft — the most systematic work of Chinese literary theory.

milestones.title: Qieyun rhyme book
milestones.detail: Lu Fayan and colleagues compile a compromise system of literary readings for poetry; its category framework is the backbone all later reconstructions of Middle Chinese hang on.

milestones.title: Dated printing: the Diamond Sutra
milestones.detail: The earliest printed book with a colophon date rolls out of a woodblock shop — a technology that will make the character a standardised, mass-reproduced object.

milestones.title: Movable type
milestones.detail: Bi Sheng develops clay movable type, described by Shen Kuo; carved woodblocks remain the workhorse of Chinese printing for centuries more.

milestones.title: The ancient-style prose ascendancy
milestones.detail: Ouyang Xiu, as chief examiner, crowns the guwen candidates; the plain, argumentative prose of the model classicists becomes the prestige written style.

milestones.title: Yunjing
milestones.detail: The earliest surviving rhyme-classification diagram arranges syllables by initial, medial and tone — Chinese phonology acquires its generator grid.

milestones.title: Zhongyuan yinyun
milestones.detail: Zhou Deqing's book of Yuefu rhymes records the living northern spoken system — level/rising/departing/entering reduced to four tones, entering tone distributed — a landmark for Mandarin historical phonology.

milestones.title: Yongzheng edict on the correct sound
milestones.detail: The court orders Zhengyin academies in Fujian and Guangdong to teach capital pronunciation to examination candidates — the empire's most systematic premodern pronunciation-standardisation drive.

milestones.title: Morrison's dictionary
milestones.detail: Robert Morrison's A Dictionary of the Chinese and English Language, printed at Malacca, begins the era of Western lexicography keyed to the vernacular.

milestones.title: Yimuliao chujie
milestones.detail: Lu Shangzhang publishes at Fuzhou an alphabetic spelling scheme for the Zhangzhou-Quanzhou Min speech, with Mandarin in view — the opening of the late-Qing alphabetic (qieyinzi) movement.

milestones.title: Wang Zhao's alphabet published
milestones.detail: Modelled on Japanese kana strokes, Wang Zhao's Guanhua hesheng zimu began circulating in Tianjin — the most politically influential of the qieyinzi schemes before 1911.

milestones.title: New Youth and the literary revolution
milestones.detail: Chen Duxiu's journal gathers the writers who will demand that the spoken language of Beijing become the vehicle of all serious literature.

milestones.title: A Madman's Diary; Zhuyin zimu promulgated
milestones.detail: Lu Xun's vernacular masterpiece appears in New Youth the same year the state issues its first national phonetic alphabet (zhuyin) for textbook use.

milestones.title: Vernacular in the schools
milestones.detail: Following the 1919 orders, the school system replaces classical compositions with baihua essays — the single decisive institutional victory of the vernacular movement.

milestones.title: Laboratory phonetics at the Academy
milestones.detail: Zhao Yuanren, Luo Changpei and colleagues at the Institute of History and Philology record Chinese dialects with graphophones, founding empirical Chinese dialectology and the five-level tone scale.

milestones.title: Latinxua
milestones.detail: A congress in Khabarovsk adopts a Latin-based Sinized writing designed with Soviet Chinese workers — the model that pushes Zhou Youguang toward the 1950s scheme.

milestones.title: Modern Chinese Dictionary of National Language
milestones.detail: The official Guoyu character dictionary establishes a Beijing-based standard for readings, becoming a reference point across the Chinese-speaking world.

milestones.title: Script-reform debate
milestones.detail: A spate of tracts on the difficulty of Chinese characters and the reform of the writing system appears around 1949; for a decade, alphabetisation seems within reach.

milestones.title: The definition of Putonghua
milestones.detail: The National Language Unification Conference defines the standard: Beijing pronunciation as the norm, northern dialects as the base, exemplary modern vernacular as the grammatical model.

milestones.title: Hanyu Pinyin fang'an approved
milestones.detail: The National People's Congress approves the Latin-based scheme chiefly drafted by Zhou Youguang; tone marks, spelling conventions and letter rules enter the schools.

milestones.title: Table of Simplified Characters
milestones.detail: The state issues 2,236 simplified forms, redrawing the graph inventory of the mainland and freezing traditional characters into heritage, calligraphy, and use beyond it.

milestones.title: Pronunciation review table
milestones.detail: The Putonghua Yidu Shenyin Biao retabulates many readings (abolishing double pronunciations such as que3 for que4); textbook and dictionary readings follow it ever since.

milestones.title: Putonghua Proficiency Test founded
milestones.detail: Language, education and broadcasting authorities jointly launch the PSC, turning pronunciation norms into scores for teachers, hosts and civil servants.

milestones.title: Promotion Week
milestones.detail: The first national Putonghua Promotion Week puts the standard language on every province's poster wall each September.

milestones.title: National Common Language and Script Law
milestones.detail: Legislation names Putonghua and the standardised character set state common language and script, and fixes occupational proficiency requirements.

milestones.title: Table of General Standard Chinese Characters
milestones.detail: 8,105 standard characters are promulgated after a decade of review — the first comprehensive standard graph list in the simplified-character era.

milestones.title: Chinese and the language model era
milestones.detail: Large language models push machine handling of Chinese — segmentation, disambiguation, style — into the daily practice of writers and teachers.
